# Lumen — Warp's Design System (full)

> Inlined version of llms.txt for agents that do a single fetch. Combines llms.txt index with the contents of AGENTS.md, the principles, the token quick-ref, and the brand brief.

> **v0.13.0 — LLM-docs version lockstep + R4 comprehensive audit (current).** New [ADR 0023](_meta/decisions/0023-llm-docs-version-lockstep-v013.md) extends the v0.12.5 SSoT pattern from the runtime UI to the LLM-facing prose docs: `scripts/release.mjs` now rewrites the "Status: v0.X.Y" chips in `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `README.md`, `USING-LUMEN.md`, and `PRIMITIVE-COVERAGE.md` in lockstep with `VERSION` and `audit-dashboard/src/lib/version.ts`. R4 caught those five files reading v0.12.5 / v0.12.6 while the runtime was at v0.12.9 — exactly the drift class the v0.12.5 runtime-UI SSoT closed at the rendered-UI layer. `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` top callouts remain hand-rewritten per release because they carry narrative prose, not just a chip. The accompanying same-day Round 4 live audit walked every route in both dark + light at 1501×812 px (Edge on Personal Mac via Claude in Chrome MCP) and classified findings — most surface-level visual / interaction defects had already been caught by R1 / R2 / R3, leaving R4 to ship the architectural docs contract. v0.12.5 — Live-audit fix pack (single-source-of-truth version constant + iconography accent-on-hover + pricing card peak-end lift + FAQ chevron unified to lucide + native `<details>` marker contract + privacy scrubs). Brand anchors unchanged from v0.12.0: Spring Green `#00FA8A` (accent, unchanged from v0.11), Obsidian `#0D0D0D` (neutral dark canvas — replaces v0.11's `#171A18` Obsidian Mint per [ADR 0020](_meta/decisions/0020-obsidian-recolor-mint-retired-v012.md)), `#E6E6E6` (light anchor / primary text on dark). v0.12.1 — Card corner-clip contract ([ADR 0021](_meta/decisions/0021-card-corner-clip-contract-v0121.md)). v0.12.2 — primary-button hover bloom dialed down ([ADR 0022](_meta/decisions/0022-hover-glow-ladder-retune-v0122.md)). v0.12.3 — Tailwind v4 arbitrary-translate fragility retired (cascade-fix to ADR 0015/0016 — position math via inline `style.left` / `style.transform`). v0.12.4 — three primitive-layer fixes (InlineTabs pill `overflow-hidden`, Combobox dropdown portaled, global `:focus-visible` gains `outline + offset` on top of soft `box-shadow` halo). v0.12.5 — five surgical fixes from a two-round live visual audit (round 1 walks routes statically, round 2 triggers every overlay): (1) new `audit-dashboard/src/lib/version.ts` hoists the user-facing version label to a single constant — every consumer reads from it; the audit caught the command palette footer reading `Lumen v0.11.13` three minor versions stale because nobody had grepped the literal — the constant retires that whole class of drift; (2) iconography hover lifts icon glyph to `text-accent` + tile border to `border-accent` (teaches "green appears at action" visually); (3) pricing card peak-end lift on landing — non-highlighted: `shadow-md` + `border-default` + `-translate-y-[1px]`; highlighted Operator: soft accent glow; (4) landing FAQ disclosure caret migrates from Unicode `▾` (U+25BE) to lucide `ChevronDown` for consistency with commerce + tool accordions, with new `.lumen-summary` + `summary.list-none` CSS rule that suppresses the native browser disclosure marker on every browser; (5) privacy scrub — real-person names (`Sokolovsky` / `Tengariya`) retired from 9 sites in 5 files, replaced with synthetic operator names (`Avery Mercer` / `Kai Morgan`). The seven principles still encode the 50ms halo effect, aggressive hierarchy, cognitive fluency, and the peak-end rule. The three v0.11 foundations (hierarchy, first-impression, micro-interactions) operationalize these. The single-accent rule (Spring Green only) is preserved verbatim across v0.11 → v0.12.5. v0.12.3 / v0.12.4 / v0.12.5 ship without new ADRs by design — they're consequential follow-ups to existing ADRs (0007 component-contract + 0009 versioning + 0015/0016 defensive primitives + 0018 brand voice + 0021 corner-clip).

> **The three v0.12.4 + two v0.12.5 patterns LLMs need to encode** (no new ADR — consequential follow-ups to ADRs 0007 + 0009 + 0015/0016 + 0018 + 0021):
> 1. **Corner-clip extends to InlineTabs pill (v0.12.4).** Any rounded-parent + square-cornered-child container needs `overflow-hidden`. The InlineTabs pill `TabsList` extends the v0.12.1 Card corner-clip pattern at the smaller-control scale.
> 2. **Floating UI portals (v0.12.4).** Any floating popover / dropdown / autocomplete must portal to `document.body` via `createPortal` + `position: fixed` + `getBoundingClientRect()` tracking — Combobox migrated from inline `<div absolute>` to portaled in v0.12.4 because inline-absolute panels get clipped by ancestor overflow contexts (Showcase frames, `<Card padding="none">`, glass surfaces, scroll containers).
> 3. **Focus rings ride `outline + box-shadow` (v0.12.4).** Global `:focus-visible` is `outline: 2px solid lime-a64; outline-offset: 1px;` PLUS the existing soft box-shadow halo — outline paints outside the layout box and is structurally immune to ancestor `overflow: hidden`, so focus rings stay visible inside corner-clipped containers (closes the v0.12.1 ADR-0021 pagination-focus regression). The `.lumen-btn-primary:focus-visible` dual-ring is unaffected — declares `outline: none` and wins via CSS specificity.
> 4. **Version constant SSoT (v0.12.5).** Every user-facing version label imports from `@/lib/version`; never hardcode the literal. Three exports for three contexts: `LUMEN_VERSION` (patch-level chips), `LUMEN_VERSION_MAJOR_MINOR` (inline references), `LUMEN_VERSION_MAJOR_MINOR_UPPER` (uppercased brand-voice tokens). Release script bumps `lib/version.ts` in lockstep with the root `VERSION` file.
> 5. **Custom accordions suppress the native marker (v0.12.5).** Every `<details>`/`<summary>` accordion that composes its own end-of-summary chevron icon gets `class="lumen-summary"` (or `list-none`) so the native browser triangle is hidden on every browser — without it the native marker doubles up with the lucide chevron.

## Inlined: principles (from design-system/00-foundations/principles.md)

**Seven** operating principles (v0.11 grew from 5 to 7), in priority order when in conflict:

1. **Engineer the first impression.** A visitor judges in 50ms; the halo effect colors everything after. Heroes answer what/who/why, ship one focal point, and pass the cold-load contract (no shift, branded chrome on first paint).
2. **Lead the eye — one focal point per section.** Aggressive hierarchy: decisively unequal visual weight, primary tier 1.5–2× the support tier. Five things at the same volume = the user hears nothing.
3. **Less, but better.** Restraint is a constraint, not a style. Cut until removing one more thing breaks meaning. One primary action per view, one disciplined accent in the system, no second loud color, no decorative gradients.
4. **Cognitive fluency over decoration.** The brain rewards what's easy to process. Easy-to-read = trustworthy = premium. Predictable layouts > clever layouts. Tabular numerics. Reading copy capped at 60–75 ch.
5. **Care is total — peak moments, end moments, every state.** The empty state, the error toast, the disabled button, the focus ring, the 404 get the same attention as the hero. Peak-end rule: people remember peaks and endings.
6. **Color is supplement, not signal.** Status meaning never lives only in hue. Pair color with a label or shape. The accent (Spring Green) is reserved for action / live / success.
7. **Decelerate; motion serves comprehension.** Default easing `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`. UI feedback ≤ 180 ms; state changes ≤ 260 ms. The LiveDot pulse is the one signature recurring animation. Honor `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Inlined: AGENTS.md hard rules

1. Never invent tokens. Add semantic aliases, never import primitives.
2. Always reference SEMANTIC tokens. `color.surface.default`, never `color.neutral.50`.
3. Component contracts validate against `_schema/component.schema.json`.
4. Every component ships a `component.json` machine contract.
5. Accessibility is WCAG 2.2 AA. Hard floor.
6. Use platform-appropriate code templates from `02-components/{name}/examples/`.
7. The Spring Green accent (#00FA8A) plays exactly one role: action / live / success.
8. Honor `prefers-reduced-motion` everywhere.
9. Never render white or near-white text on the spring-green accent surface — use `color.accent.fg` (#07120D, 14.7:1 AAA on #00FA8A).
10. **Floating UI portals to `document.body`** (v0.12.4). Combobox / Select / DropdownMenu / Popover / Tooltip / Calendar dropdowns must escape ancestor overflow contexts via `createPortal` (or Radix Portal). Never render a floating panel as an inline `<div absolute>` — Showcase frames, `<Card padding="none">`, glass surfaces, and scroll containers all clip it. The portal pattern: `createPortal(<div style={{ position: 'fixed', top, left, width, zIndex }} />, document.body)` with `getBoundingClientRect()` re-tracked on scroll (capture phase) + resize. Outside-click dismiss must exempt the portaled list, since clicks on options would otherwise close the dropdown before the option handler fires.
11. **Focus rings ride `outline + box-shadow`, not box-shadow alone** (v0.12.4). The global `:focus-visible` rule is `outline: 2px solid var(--lumen-lime-a64); outline-offset: 1px;` PLUS the existing soft `box-shadow: var(--shadow-focus)` glow halo. Outline is painted outside the layout box and is structurally immune to ancestor `overflow: hidden` (so focus rings stay visible inside `<Card padding="none">` and other corner-clipped containers); box-shadow paints the brand-defining soft halo when unclipped. Modern browsers (Chrome 94+, Firefox 88+, Safari 16.4+) follow `border-radius` for outline when `outline-style` is not `auto`. The `.lumen-btn-primary:focus-visible` dual-ring is unaffected — it declares `outline: none` and wins via CSS specificity (preserves ADR 0016's brand visual). Do NOT write a new `:focus-visible` rule with `box-shadow` only.
12. **Position math via inline `style`, not Tailwind arbitrary classes** (v0.12.3). Tailwind v4's content scanner has been observed to drop arbitrary `translate-x-[Npx]` / `top-[Npx]` / `left-[Npx]` utilities (intermittent, scanner-dependent — `getComputedStyle` reports `none` despite the className carrying it). For thumb / swipe / handle / popover anchor position math, use inline `style={{ left: N, transform: 'translateX(...)' }}` with a native `transition` declaration. Inline style is scanner-independent (the rule is on the element, not bundled CSS the scanner has to discover). Same `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` decelerate easing as the rest of the system. The defensive `.lumen-btn-*` and `.lumen-field` class families per ADRs 0015/0016 remain the canonical pattern for component STYLING; rule 12 is specifically about position MATH on toggles, switches, swipe rows, calendar nav, etc.

13. **Version labels read from `lib/version.ts`, never hardcoded literals** (v0.12.5). Every user-facing version label — header pill, footer line, command-palette footer, foundations brand-voice samples, library / tool / foundations badges, "End of library — last refreshed" line — imports from `audit-dashboard/src/lib/version.ts`. Three exports cover three contexts: `LUMEN_VERSION` (`"v0.12.5"`) for patch-level chips; `LUMEN_VERSION_MAJOR_MINOR` (`"v0.12"`) for inline mono-cap references that don't need the patch; `LUMEN_VERSION_MAJOR_MINOR_UPPER` (`"V0.12"`) for explicitly-uppercased brand-voice tokens (`SYSTEM V0.12 · LIVE`). The release script bumps both `VERSION` and `lib/version.ts` in lockstep. Exemptions: prose descriptions of historical versions ("v0.10 retired JetBrains Mono"), ADR titles / filenames, CSS / TSX comments documenting when a rule landed — those stay literal. The constant is for current-version labels rendered in the runtime UI, not for prose history. Pre-v0.12.5 the labels drifted (v0.11.13 in the palette footer while the rest of the system read v0.12.4 — three minor versions stale); the constant retires that whole class.

14. **`<details>`/`<summary>` accordions suppress the native disclosure marker — always — when composing your own end-of-summary chevron** (v0.12.5). When you write a Lumen accordion that paints its own affordance icon at the END of the summary (the canonical pattern: lucide `ChevronDown size={14}` rotating 180° via `group-open:rotate-180` on the summary), the native browser-default disclosure triangle (▶/▼ in webkit, ▾/▸ in firefox) STILL renders before the summary's text content — two arrows compete for affordance, only one of them on the brand stroke ladder. The `globals.css` `.lumen-summary` + `summary.list-none` rule suppresses both: `list-style: none` covers modern Chrome / Safari / Firefox via the standard `::marker`; `::-webkit-details-marker { display: none }` covers the pre-2022 webkit fallback. Apply the class on every accordion summary that composes a custom chevron (Tailwind `list-none` triggers the same rule pair).

## Inlined: token quick reference

### Surfaces (v0.12 — neutral obsidian, mint retired)
- `color.surface.page` — page canvas (paper-clean off-white #FAFAFA in light, neutral obsidian #0D0D0D in dark — was #171A18 obsidian-mint pre-v0.12)
- `color.surface.raised` — cards (white in light, raised obsidian #151515 in dark — was #1B1E1C pre-v0.12)
- `color.surface.popover` — dropdowns / menus (neutral obsidian #1F1F1F in dark — was #232624 pre-v0.12)
- `color.surface.sunken` — inputs, table row hover (anchored to user-fixed #E6E6E6 in light)
- `color.surface.overlay` — translucent sticky chrome
- `color.surface.inverse` — dark surface for contrast moments

### Text
- `color.text.primary` — body and titles (17.2:1 light / 13.7:1 dark)
- `color.text.secondary` — captions (10.5:1 / 6.4:1)
- `color.text.tertiary` — hints (5.4:1 / 3.6:1 ≥18px only)
- `color.text.inverse` — text on inverse surfaces
- `color.text.accent` — emphasis text matching accent

### Action
- `color.action.primary.bg.{rest,hover,press}` — Spring Green button background (#00FA8A → #00D675 → #00B062)
- `color.action.primary.fg` — near-black text on accent (#07120D, 14.7:1 AAA on the spring-green surface)
- `shadow.button.glow.{rest,hover,active}` — three-state glow ladder for primary CTAs. v0.12.2 retune (rest unchanged on purpose — that's the brand voice; hover dialed down — the bloom-too-much fix):
  - rest:   `0 0 16px var(--lumen-lime-a25)` (unchanged across v0.11 / v0.12 / v0.12.2)
  - hover:  `0 0 20px var(--lumen-lime-a28)` (was `0 0 24px lime-a40` pre-v0.12.2)
  - active: `0 0 8px  var(--lumen-lime-a20)` (unchanged)
- Primary `:hover` layered halo (when `@media (hover: hover) and prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`):
  - layer 1: `var(--shadow-button-glow-hover)` (the token above)
  - layer 2: `0 0 20px var(--lumen-lime-a14)` (was `24px lime-a20` pre-v0.12.2 — the "lit boost" middle layer)
  - layer 3: `0 0 32px var(--lumen-lime-a08)` (was `48px lime-a10` pre-v0.12.2 — the wide "bloom" outer layer)
- `.lumen-glow-cta:hover` — hero-CTA-only halo (landing page money buttons, `lumen-glow-cta` class only). v0.12.2 trimmed in lockstep so hero still reads ~1.5× standard primary.

### Status
- `color.status.{success,warning,danger,info}.{bg,fg}` — always paired with label or shape, never color alone

### Spacing (semantic)
- `space.0` to `space.32` (4-based scale)
- `space.stack.{xs,sm,md,lg,xl}` — vertical rhythm
- `space.inline.{xs,sm,md,lg}` — horizontal gaps
- `space.section.{sm,md,lg,xl}` — between major page sections

### Radius
- `radius.control.md` — buttons, inputs (6 px)
- `radius.card.default` — cards (10 px)
- `radius.card.lifted` — interactive cards (14 px)
- `radius.card.hero` — hero surfaces (20 px)
- `radius.pill` — status badges, dots

### Motion
- `motion.transition.fast` — 120 ms standard (hover, micro-feedback)
- `motion.transition.base` — 180 ms standard (default UI feedback)
- `motion.transition.slow` — 260 ms standard (state changes)
- `motion.transition.page` — 400 ms standard (page transitions)
- `motion.easing.standard` — `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` (default)
- `motion.easing.decelerate` — entry side
- `motion.easing.accelerate` — exit side

### Typography
- `type.display.{xl,lg,md}` — hero, section opener, page title (76/49/39 px)
- `type.heading.{h1,h2,h3}` — app title, section, subsection (31/25/20 px)
- `type.body.{lg,md,sm}` — lead, default, secondary (18/16/14 px)
- `type.caption` (13 px) — metadata
- `type.micro` (12 px) — eyebrows, badges
- `type.label.{sm,eyebrow}` — UI labels
- `type.code.{inline,block}` — Satoshi with `calt 1, liga 1, zero 1` (v0.10 — JetBrains Mono retired)

## Inlined: brand brief decisions (v0.11 current)

### D-001 Visual mood
Quiet Industrial — Obsidian (v0.12, mint retired). Warp's substance + Apple's typographic discipline + Premium Psychology principles. Paper-clean off-white in light, neutral near-black in dark (true neutral, R = G = B at every dark stop). v0.11's Obsidian Mint anchor `#171A18` was retired in v0.12 in favour of neutral `#0D0D0D` per ADR 0020 — the canvas no longer carries a hue, so the spring-green accent has the hue stage to itself.

### D-002 Color (v0.12 — Obsidian recolor, mint retired)
Spring Green `#00FA8A` as the only loud color, role: action / live / success (unchanged from v0.11). Hover `#00D675`, press `#00B062`. Light mode canvas `#FAFAFA` (paper-clean). Dark mode canvas `#0D0D0D` (neutral obsidian — replaces v0.11's `#171A18` obsidian-mint with its faint G+2 channel undertone; v0.12 strips the tilt across every dark stop). Raised dark surface `#151515` (was `#1B1E1C` pre-v0.12). Popover dark surface `#1F1F1F` (was `#232624` pre-v0.12). Primary text on dark = `#E6E6E6` (the user-fixed brand light), not pure white. Status hues unchanged from v0.11 (refined danger `#E5484D`, warning `#F5B118`). The single-accent rule is preserved verbatim. See ADR 0018 (premium-psychology rationale, amended by ADR 0020), ADR 0020 (obsidian recolor — mint retired).

### D-003 Typography (v0.10 current)
Satoshi alone. UI, display, body, numerics, code, editorial — single typeface, separated by weight/size/tracking + OpenType feature flags. 1.25 modular scale on 16 px base. (v0.10 retired JetBrains Mono, Source Serif 4, Inter — see ADR 0017.)

### D-004 Spacing & geometry
4-based spacing scale, 8-pt soft grid. Radius 2/4/6/10/14/20/28/9999. Hairline borders do most surface separation. Marketing breathes (96 px hero rhythm) · Operator stays dense (24 px section rhythm).

### D-005 Motion
Decelerate, don't bounce. Default easing `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`. UI ≤ 180 ms. The LiveDot pulse is the one signature loop. Peak-end rule guides the micro-interaction catalog (see `micro-interactions.md`).

### D-006 Imagery
No stock photography. Marketing: product screenshots first, documentary second. No mascots, no illustrated scenes. Iconography: Lucide, 1.5 px stroke, 24 px grid, rounded ends.

### D-007 Density (v0.11, unchanged in v0.12.x)
Marketing surfaces breathe; operator surfaces stay dense. 1100 px primary marketing width, 1440–1920 px operator width. Tables compact 32 px rows. Both express calm-confidence — at different cadences.

### D-008 Hierarchy (v0.11 new)
Aggressive — one focal point per section, primary tier 1.5–2× the support tier. Equal-weight noise reads cheap.

### D-009 First impression (v0.11 new)
Engineered. The 50ms contract: hero answers what/who/why and passes three halo checks (branded chrome, single focal point, no layout shift) before the user scrolls.

### D-010 Live-data signature primitives
Three: `Stat` (big tabular numeric + small unit), `LiveDot` (8 px spring-green dot with 2 px pulsing ring), `RateTicker` (horizontal scrolling lane rates).

### D-011 Card corner-clip contract (v0.12.1 — new)
`<Card padding="none">` automatically clips its edge-touching children to the rounded corner via `overflow-hidden`. Without the clip, a child with its own background and square corners (table header row, pagination footer row, full-bleed product image) would paint past the curved interior and poke a visible square nub out from behind the rounded border. Other padding tiers don't need it — their `p-N` insets float children off the curved edge. Radix-portaled popovers, dropdowns, and tooltips render outside the Card subtree and are unaffected. See ADR 0021. The user screenshot that motivated the fix: the `/saas` Pagination "Next" button stair-stepping past the bottom-right of the Shipments card.

### D-012 Hover-glow ladder retune (v0.12.2 — new)
Primary-button hover bloom dialed down at the token + layered-halo level. Rest stays at `0 0 16px lime-a25` (the always-present brand "lit" signal — that's the brand voice, see ADR 0018). Hover trims to `0 0 20px lime-a28` (was `0 0 24px lime-a40`). The layered halo middle layer trims to `0 0 20px lime-a14` (was `0 0 24px lime-a20`). The wide outer layer — the user-reported "bloom edge" — trims to `0 0 32px lime-a08` (was `0 0 48px lime-a10`). Active stays at `0 0 8px lime-a20`. `.lumen-glow-cta:hover` (hero CTAs only) trimmed in lockstep so the standard-vs-hero hierarchy stays intact (~1.5× spread on hero). Spring-green RGB and alpha primitives unchanged — the dial-down moves the *composition* of glow layers, not the underlying alpha tier values. See ADR 0022.

### D-013 Inline-style position math retires Tailwind arbitrary translate (v0.12.3 — new)
Tailwind v4's content scanner is unreliable with arbitrary `translate-x-[Npx]` classes — `getComputedStyle` reports `none` despite the className carrying the utility (intermittent, scanner-dependent). PricingToggle and SwipeAction (the last two callers of arbitrary-translate position math in the codebase) migrated to inline `style.left` / `style.transform` + native `transition: left 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`. Inline style is scanner-independent (the rule is on the element, not bundled CSS the scanner has to discover); explicit `left` overrides the static-position fallback (no `auto`, no centering surprise on `<button>` elements with default `text-align: center`). Cascade-fix to ADRs 0015/0016 — the same defensive-pattern reasoning that retired shadcn bridge utilities for buttons (`bg-primary` → `.lumen-btn-primary`) now retires arbitrary-translate utilities for toggle/swipe position math. The Lumen Switch primitive at `audit-dashboard/src/components/ui/switch.tsx` already used the defensive `.lumen-switch` CSS class system; PricingToggle was the outlier that bypassed the defensive pattern, SwipeAction the latent second site. Rule for new toggle / handle / swipe primitives: position math via inline style or via a `.lumen-{primitive}` defensive class system; never via Tailwind arbitrary classes.

### D-014 Card corner-clip pattern extends to InlineTabs pill (v0.12.4 — new)
The corner-clip pattern from ADR 0021 (rounded parent + child with its own background and square corners + `overflow: visible` = visible square nub poking past the rounded corner) is not Card-specific. v0.12.4 applies the same `overflow-hidden` recipe to the `TabsList` for the InlineTabs `pill` variant: the active tab carries `data-[state=active]:bg-[var(--surface-raised)]` with `radius-md` corners inside a parent with `radius-lg`; without the clip the active pill's smaller-radius square corners poke past the parent's larger-radius curve, reading as a visible step at the bottom-left when active. The fix lives at the `TabsList` level (not on the active tab) so each layer keeps its own rounded contract: parent has `rounded-lg`, active pill has `rounded-md`, parent clips the pill's square corners to its own curved shape. Same reasoning as ADR 0021 for Cards: the contract is "child clips to parent's rounded shape," not "child matches parent's radius." LLM rule: any rounded container hosting children with their own backgrounds and smaller-radius corners needs `overflow-hidden` on the parent.

### D-015 Floating UI portals to document.body (v0.12.4 — new)
Combobox migrated its dropdown from inline `<div absolute z-[var(--z-overlay)] left-0 right-0 mt-1 ...>` to `createPortal(<div style={{ position: 'fixed', top, left, width, zIndex }}>, document.body)` with `getBoundingClientRect()` re-tracked on scroll (capture phase) + resize. The portal escapes every ancestor's overflow context — works inside `Showcase` demo frames, inside `<Card padding="none">` (which has `overflow: hidden` per ADR 0021), inside any nested flex/grid cell with overflow-clip, anywhere. Outside-click dismiss exempts the portaled list (since clicks on options would otherwise close the dropdown before the option handler fires). The Lumen `Switch`, `Tooltip`, `DropdownMenu`, `Popover`, `Dialog` already portal via Radix; Combobox was the outlier hand-rolled primitive that inherited from a pre-portal era — v0.12.4 brought it in line. LLM rule: any new floating panel (autocomplete, popover, calendar, menu, suggestion list) portals to `document.body` from day one. Don't bet on the consumer never embedding it inside an overflow-clipped ancestor.

### D-016 Focus rings: outline + box-shadow, not box-shadow alone (v0.12.4 — new)
Pre-v0.12.4 the global `:focus-visible` rule used `box-shadow: var(--shadow-focus)` only. Box-shadow paints into the element's own painting context which DOES respect ancestor `overflow: hidden` — so focus rings on Pagination buttons inside `<Card padding="none">` (per ADR 0021) were partially clipped by the corner-clip rule, producing the user-reported "underline + vertical bar" fragments at the bottom of the Shipments card. v0.12.4 adds `outline: 2px solid var(--lumen-lime-a64); outline-offset: 1px;` to the global rule, with the existing box-shadow halo retained as a soft outer glow. Outline is painted outside the layout box and is structurally unaffected by ancestor overflow. Modern browsers (Chrome 94+, Firefox 88+, Safari 16.4+) follow `border-radius` for outline when `outline-style` is not `auto`. The `.lumen-btn-primary:focus-visible` rule already declares `outline: none` and overrides via CSS specificity, so the dual-ring brand visual on primary buttons stays as ADR 0016 designed it. Belt + braces: the outline guarantees the focus indicator is ALWAYS visible as a structural ring (immune to ancestor overflow); the box-shadow paints the soft alpha-blended halo for the brand voice (when unclipped). LLM rule: a `:focus-visible` rule must include `outline` for structural visibility, then layer `box-shadow` for the brand halo. Box-shadow alone fails inside corner-clipped ancestors; outline alone loses the soft brand character.

### D-017 Architecture
DTCG JSON tokens → Style Dictionary v5 → 9 platform outputs. Three-layer taxonomy. Two-file-per-component (md + json). shadcn registry distribution. Layered LLM contract.

### D-018 Single-source-of-truth version constant (v0.12.5 — new)
`audit-dashboard/src/lib/version.ts` exports `LUMEN_VERSION` (`"v0.12.5"`), `LUMEN_VERSION_MAJOR_MINOR` (`"v0.12"`), and `LUMEN_VERSION_MAJOR_MINOR_UPPER` (`"V0.12"`). Every user-facing version label in the runtime UI — header pill, footer line, command-palette footer, foundations brand-voice samples, library / tool / foundations badges, "End of library — last refreshed" line — imports from this module. Pre-v0.12.5 these labels were hardcoded per-file and drifted independently — the v0.11.13 → v0.12.4 audit found the command palette footer reading `Lumen v0.11.13` three minor versions stale because no one had grepped the literal. The constant retires that whole class of cross-file drift. The release script (`scripts/release.mjs`) bumps both the root `VERSION` file and `lib/version.ts` in lockstep on every `pnpm release patch|minor|major`. Exemptions: prose descriptions of historical versions ("v0.10 retired JetBrains Mono"), ADR titles / filenames, CSS / TSX comments documenting when a rule landed all stay literal. The constant is for *current-version labels rendered in the runtime UI*, not for *prose history*. LLM rule: before rendering any version string in TSX, import from `@/lib/version`.

### D-019 Iconography accent-on-hover micro-interaction (v0.12.5 — new)
Interactive icon tiles (foundations §08 Iconography demo, icon picker grids, quick-action tiles, single-icon button cards) hover-state lifts the icon glyph color from `var(--text-primary)` → `var(--text-accent)` and the tile border from `var(--border-hairline)` → `var(--border-accent)` on the 140 ms `motion-fast` curve, in addition to the existing `var(--surface-tint-accent)` background tint. Pre-v0.12.5 the hover only tinted the background — the icon stayed neutral, leaving the brand rule "green appears precisely at action" (foundations §Color "Accent in context") taught only in prose. Per Premium Psychology principle 3: micro-interactions are the place users *feel* the system, not where they read it. The hover state IS the action — accent appearing on hover IS the rule materializing. LLM rule: every interactive icon tile composes the three-property hover transition.

### D-020 Pricing card peak-end lift (v0.12.5 — new)
Interactive cards at peak decision moments (pricing tier selection, plan picker, primary action card, decision tile) gain hover lift via the existing system tokens. Non-highlighted cards: `hover:shadow-[var(--shadow-md)] hover:border-[var(--border-default)] hover:-translate-y-[1px]`. Highlighted cards (the Operator tier in the canonical landing pricing pattern): layer `var(--shadow-glow-accent)` on top of the rest-state lifted shadow. 140 ms standard easing, decelerate-not-bounce per ADR 0016 — no marketing-deck bounce. Per Premium Psychology principle 3 (peak-end rule): the pricing decision IS a peak moment; the cards must respond at the moment of decision, not stay static. Static peak-moment cards are an LLM-UI smell — the model knows the cards exist but doesn't know they're peak moments. LLM rule: any card that wraps a primary CTA at a decision moment composes hover lift.

### D-021 Accordion summary marker contract (v0.12.5 — new)
`<details>`/`<summary>` accordions that compose their own end-of-summary chevron icon (the canonical Lumen accordion pattern: lucide `ChevronDown size={14}` rotating 180° via `group-open:rotate-180`) MUST suppress the native browser disclosure triangle, which otherwise renders BEFORE the summary text — producing two competing arrows, only one of them on the brand stroke ladder. The `globals.css` `.lumen-summary` + `summary.list-none` rule covers all browsers: `list-style: none` for modern Chrome / Safari / Firefox via standard `::marker`, `::-webkit-details-marker { display: none }` for pre-2022 webkit fallback. Apply on every accordion summary. Pre-v0.12.5 the landing FAQ used Unicode `▾` (U+25BE BLACK DOWN-POINTING SMALL TRIANGLE) instead of the lucide icon, mismatching the commerce + tool accordion chevrons; v0.12.5 unified the icon language and added the marker-contract rule. LLM rule: every new custom accordion summary gets `class="lumen-summary"` (or `list-none`) plus a lucide `<ChevronDown />` (or other appropriate lucide affordance icon) at the end.
